stem: Meena and Arjun measure the length of the same study table at home using their own handspans. Meena counts 8 handspans and Arjun counts 10 handspans. Which statement correctly explains why their answers are different?

options.text: Arjun counted more handspans, so the table must be longer when he measures it.
Their answers in centimetres would also be different, because a centimetre is a different length for each student.
Meena is shorter than Arjun, so she must have counted fewer handspans.
Handspans differ in size from person to person, so the same table can give different counts.

teacher.key_rationale: A measurement number depends on the length of the unit used. Since handspans are body-part units that vary between people, Meena's and Arjun's different counts for the same table are explained by their different handspan sizes, not by any change in the table. A reverses the relation, B wrongly treats the standard centimetre as person-dependent, and C uses a surface feature (height) rather than handspan size.
